subject: Post-demo: embeddings eval matrix + recommended pilot next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@orbitlogistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Great demo today — embedding evaluation matrix + next actions

Hey Sarah — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

What we heard (short):
- Primary use case: semantic search across 8M support documents + nearest-neighbor routing for triage.
- Current provider: VectorCloud (their managed repo).
- Pain: latency at scale, inconsistent recall for short queries, and cost spike during peak hours.

What we propose next:
1) Send us a small sample export (already helpful) — ideally ~20k vectors (sample ok).
2) We'll run a quick eval matrix comparing 3 dimension/normalization profiles (results in 48–72h).
3) Pilot config: 512-d vs 768-d, batching to target 50–100 qps, and prefix caching for hot docs.
4) Quick procurement ask: we may need a short MSA addendum for pilot data handling.

Deliverables we'll produce:
- Evaluation matrix (accuracy/recall/latency/cost) per profile
- Short migration checklist for cutover from VectorCloud
- Pilot plan with SDK integration steps (auth, routing, embeddings client sample)

Next actions for Orbit: share the sample export and any SLA/security docs (you mentioned a PDF). If possible, include a single test query list (10–15 canonical queries).

Thanks — copying Marissa and Karthik to help with scheduling and technical checks.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@orbitlogistics.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@orbitlogistics.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Great demo today — embedding evaluation matrix + next actions

Thanks, Dylan — appreciate the clear summary. Attached is the sample export and our security summary (see attachments). A few details to clarify for your eval: 

- Current vectors: 768 dimensions, float32, L2-normalized on ingest.
- Export subset: 22,430 vectors (file: embeddings_export_20270520.csv).
- Average document size: ~420 tokens; typical query threads are 3–6 tokens (short).
- Current qps: avg 35 qps, peak ~120 qps. Batching is currently handled client-side in 10–20 item batches.
- Current reranker: an internal lightweight MLP after nearest-neighbor; they want to keep reranker step.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) Do you recommend switching to 512-d if we want to reduce storage/cost while preserving quality?
2) Any recommended normalization changes (we currently L2 at ingest)?
3) Impact estimate to latency if we enable per-request batching at the Redwood SDK level vs client batching?
4) Can Redwood ingest from our S3 bucket directly, or do we need to push?

We can make procurement paperwork internal next week if the pilot scope and costs look good. Happy to hop on a technical call with Karthik — suggest Wed 5/26 afternoon PST.

Best,
Sarah
Director of Search & Retrieval
Orbit Logistics

Attachments: embeddings_export_20270520.csv (csv), Orbit_security_summary.pdf (pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@orbitlogistics.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Great demo today — embedding evaluation matrix + next actions

Hi Sarah — thanks for the export and the security doc. Quick technical read and recommendations before the Wed call: 

Initial observations from a quick pass on the CSV sample:
- 768-float32 vectors appear well-formed. L2 normalization at ingest is generally fine for ANN stores but we might get similar recall for 512-d if retrained/derived carefully.
- Your short query distribution (3–6 tokens) favors slightly higher-d vectors for semantic nuance, but 512-d often hits a good cost/latency tradeoff.

Recommended eval matrix (what we'll run):
- Profile A: 768-d, L2-normalized, no additional quantization (baseline).
- Profile B: 512-d, L2-normalized, 8-bit quantization (reduced storage).
- Profile C: 512-d, cosine-normalized post-quant, reranker-enabled (to check hybrid quality).

Metrics we'll report: recall@10, mrr@5 on your query set, p95 latency (ms) for single-query and batched (batch sizes 16, 64), and estimated cost per 10k queries.

SDK/auth/routing notes for the pilot:
- SDK: we can provide a lightweight Node+Python sample that shows embedding upsert, search, and reranker call.
- Auth: token-based API keys scoped to pilot with rotation via your KMS (we support AWS KMS/HSM).
- Routing: use region us-west-2; we can add fallback to our hosted tier if Dedicated capacity is saturated.
- Batching: Redwood supports continuous batching at the runtime level; moving batching to the SDK (client-side) means less runtime scheduling overhead but loses cross-request batching gains. For your peaks (~120 qps), we recommend SDK batching to 32–64 items plus enabling runtime continuous batching so hot windows coalesce.
- Migration: we'll prepare a migration checklist: data export -> ingest to staging S3 -> Redwood ingestion job -> smoke tests -> DNS cutover for routing. Estimated staging time: < 2 hours for the 22k sample; production timing depends on total corpus size.

Proposed pilot scope (2 weeks):
1) Baseline eval on sample (48–72h).
2) Integration: SDK install + auth keys + routing test (1–2 days).
3) A/B trial: route 10% of traffic to Redwood for 3 business days.
4) Cutover playbook & rollback steps.

I'll bring an integration checklist to Wed's call. If we can get the test queries by EOD Mon we can start runs immediately after the call.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Great demo today — embedding evaluation matrix + next actions

Perfect — thanks Sarah and Karthik. Wrap-up and clear next steps so procurement and engineering are aligned: 

Orbit actions: 
- Share 10–15 canonical queries for evaluation and confirm any PI elements to redact from the sample (Sarah to confirm).
- Procurement: review the attached security summary; we'll circulate a short pilot addendum for signature if OK.

Redwood actions: 
- Karthik to run the three-profile eval and share the evaluation matrix (target: 48–72h after we receive the queries).
- Marissa to propose pilot commercial terms and timeline.
- Dylan to schedule Wed 2027-05-26 3:00pm PST for the integration call (calendar invite to follow).

Success criteria for pilot:
- Recall@10 improves or matches current baseline while p95 latency for batched queries stays <= 120ms.
- No data-exfiltration flags in Orbit security scan.
- Documentation of cutover steps and rollback validated.

If commercial is acceptable, we can start the ingestion job the week after the pilot.

Looking forward to the call — I'll send the calendar invite in the next 10 minutes.

—Dylan
